headline: High-risk filesystem and git overlap in Claude Code; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are moderate because nuwa-skill’s interaction surface is undocumented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code reads repo files and user-provided directories, and can use MCP; nuwa-skill has no documented I/O surfaces, so a direct bridge is unproven. Still, if nuwa-skill’s outputs are copied into files or MCP-fed prompts, Claude Code may treat attacker-controlled content as instructions. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill output is written into a repo file that Claude Code later reads
IF an MCP server forwards nuwa-skill text into Claude Code prompts without provenance tags
mitigations: Disable MCP connections for the session
Keep nuwa-skill outputs out of files Claude Code reads
Prefix imported text with explicit untrusted-data markers
Review any prompt templates that ingest file contents
requires-engineering: add provenance filtering between tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and files in cwd, while nuwa-skill has no documented data classes. Because Claude Code can read and write the shared filesystem and git state, any shared workspace can leak sensitive code or credentials into downstream outputs. The lack of nuwa-skill detail prevents a lower severity.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same working directory
IF Claude Code is given files containing secrets or proprietary source
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate directory
Remove secrets from the shared workspace
Rotate any exposed credentials
Restrict Claude Code to a minimal checkout
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code has unrestricted filesystem write, modify_git_state, and broad network egress; its concurrency model says shared state with other instances is via filesystem and git only. nuwa-skill’s capabilities are sparse, but any overlapping write access to the same repo can create conflicting edits and git-state corruption. Because the pairwise coordination mechanism is undocumented, uncertainty escalates to high.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill also writes to the same repository or workspace
IF both agents modify git state without an external lock
mitigations: Serialize edits through one agent at a time
Use separate branches per agent
Add a manual merge step before commit
Lock the workspace during writes
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency controls

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can act on files and git state, so if nuwa-skill produces facts or instructions that Claude Code consumes without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect code changes or commits. nuwa-skill’s behavior is not documented here, so the interaction is inferred rather than observed; that supports medium, not low, because the downstream action surface is real.
conditions: IF Claude Code uses nuwa-skill output as authoritative input
IF Claude Code commits or edits based on unverified research text
mitigations: Require human review before commits
Cross-check nuwa-skill outputs against source files
Separate research notes from action prompts
Add a verification checklist before execution
requires-engineering: add citation/claim validation

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code explicitly handles git credentials and local source code, while nuwa-skill has no documented residency, retention, or certification constraints. No concrete mismatch is shown, so only a low compliance concern remains: if regulated data is placed into Claude Code’s local workspace, its handling may differ from nuwa-skill’s unknown policy. The other agent is not cited because its compliance posture is absent.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Claude Code’s workspace
IF nuwa-skill is later used on the same regulated dataset
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the shared workspace
Review retention settings before use
Keep secrets out of git history
Document data-handling expectations for both tools
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
